title: FLA import: decode Media N streams to populate BitmapItem.dataUri and place bitmap instances
description:
## Problem
When importing a real Flash 8 .fla that contains imported bitmaps, all bitmap content is silently dropped. The OLE2 extractor reads ALL streams (including 'Media N') into a Map<string, Uint8Array> (ole.ts line 400–409), and CPicBitmapRef records carry a mediaId (u16) pointing to the correct 'Media N' stream (flash8-binary.ts:1497). But flash8-import.ts hits the 'bitmap' case (line 553–556) and warns 'bitmap placements are not imported (Media stream decoding unsupported); skipping'. Neither BitmapItem library entries nor bitmap DisplayObjects are created.

## What's needed

### 1. Parse Media N stream headers
Each 'Media N' OLE stream is a CArchive-serialized media payload. The header encodes the media type (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.) and raw image bytes. Research format using the JPEXS flacomdoc Java source and eddiemoore/fla-decoder Ghidra notes (both referenced in CLAUDE.md). The mediaId in CPicBitmapRef maps to the 'Media ${mediaId}' stream name.

### 2. Extract raw image bytes -> data URI
Once the header is parsed, extract the raw JPEG/PNG bytes and encode as data:image/jpeg;base64,... or data:image/png;base64,... data URIs.

### 3. Build BitmapItem library entries
During buildFla8Document (flash8-import.ts), iterate all 'Media N' streams from the map, parse each, create a BitmapItem (createBitmap from @flash/core) with the decoded dataUri, and populate a mediaIdToLibraryItemId Map<number, string> lookup.

### 4. Wire CPicBitmapRef -> bitmap DisplayObject
In the element-to-DisplayObject mapping (flash8-import.ts), the 'bitmap' case currently skips. Using the mediaIdToLibraryItemId map, create a bitmap-type DisplayObject ({ type: 'bitmap', libraryItemId, x, y, scaleX, scaleY }) from the CPicBitmapRef matrix decomposition and mediaId.

## Acceptance criteria
- Import a real Flash 8 .fla fixture with at least one imported JPEG bitmap.
- The resulting document's library.items contains a BitmapItem with a valid dataUri (non-empty, correct MIME type, parseable as image).
- The scene timeline contains a bitmap DisplayObject referencing that BitmapItem.
- Publishing the imported document to SWF produces a SWF that passes the existing bitmap-rendering e2e test (apps/desktop/e2e/bitmap-rendering.spec.ts).
- Add a unit test in packages/core/src/fla/__tests__/ covering the Media stream parse path.

## References
- packages/core/src/fla/ole.ts (stream extraction, line 398–409)
- packages/core/src/fla/flash8-binary.ts (readCPicBitmapRef line 1489; Fla8BitmapRef line 182)
- packages/core/src/fla/flash8-import.ts (bitmap skip warning line 553–556; buildFla8Document line 674)
- CLAUDE.md 'Binary FLA import' learnings for format reference pointers
